en: Kiyokawa?
Yeah? What's up?
I need you to come with me.
Huh? Oh, okay. Gladly.
There's that client calling from the highway rest area again. He's asking for you, Suzuki-san.
(Then it must be the Devil Killers.)
Might I add, he's being very polite, too.
(Sounds like Cool Yoshimi, one of the Four Kings.)
Then I'll make sure to leave a strong impression.
You're not gettin' away today.
Forget it, I'm not gonna study! Any more of these meaningless words and symbols and I'm gonna lose my marbles!
The chief asked us to help Kiyokawa-kun study for his driver's test.
Yeah, and he ain't exactly the bookworm type. Furthest thing from it, actually.

Come on, what does memorizing a bunch of random rules have
to do with driving a car?

I mean, I already know how to drive, so just let me loose
on the road! It's not like I'm gonna smash into anyone.
It doesn't matter how good you are at driving. To be a taxi driver, you need a Class 2 license. And that requires a certain amount of studying.
Argh! You say that, but I still don't wanna believe it!
Better start showing some effort, or you'll be stuck on the written test forever.
Yeah, and might I remind you, this is taking up our time too! I'm using up my breaks to teach you, so hurry up and get it through your head!
I can't! I've never been good at bookwork. Even if I studied night and day, I still wouldn't pass!
Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaagh! I hate it! Just lemme get behind the wheel with my foot on the pedal already!
Don't forget your seatbelt first.
Gah! That's it! I'm done with this!
He made a run for it.

Sheesh. They're way too easy on kids in school these days.
They all end up like him.
Sorry he's being such a pain to both of you.
No need to apologize, Suzuki-kun. It's not your fault.
Well, I'm the one who got him hired. I can at least go bring him back.
Good luck with that. Who knows where he's gone to now?
I have a pretty good idea. Just sit tight for a bit.
Well hello, hello! Good to see you show up! Am I going to have to do this a hundred more times until you finally catch a lucky break?
Cool Yoshimi!
Listen, Suzuki-san. I know this is a tricky concept for a simpleton like you, but statistics show your defeat is inevitable. You really don't stand a chance.
Enough talk. Let's get this started.
There's no point, Suzuki-san! You're only gonna lose again!
The kid's got it right. He must be smarter than you. But, have it your way. Let's do a rematch.
See if you can at least make it close!
Suzuki-san! What're you doing here? Did you come looking for me?
Well, don't try and drag me back with you. I've had it with studying.
A knucklehead like me probably only has a one in a hundred chance of passing. I don't wanna fight a losing battle.
No, I have other business here.
You mean... another race with the Devil Killers?
You're up against Cool Yoshimi this time, right? I know you don't wanna hear this, but I think you should just bow out now, to be honest.
I'm on your side, of course. But I know what he's capable of. You don't stand a chance, man.
(Not with that attitude, anyway.)
That Crash Kajiwara guy you beat, he's the bottom of the ladder when it comes to the Four Kings. Cool Yoshimi is on a whole 'nother level.
He's that fast, huh?
Yep. Yoshimi wins all his races 'cause he's sharp as a tack, and never loses his cool.
When you go up against him, you can bet that he already knows your ride down to every last nut and bolt. He's that thorough.
He works up a profile of you, and compares it with all the data he's gathered to figure out the best way to win.
(Kiyokawa sure knows a lot. He should devote a little of that brainpower to studying.)
Anyway! I think you gotta cut your losses here. I don't wanna see you go down in flames.
It's just like my studying. It'd be stupid to take on something you just can't win.
Good to see you, Suzuki-san.
Whoa! It's Cool Yoshimi!
I hear you like studying up on your opponents.
That's right. This time was tougher than usual. It's my first race against a taxi, for one. I didn't have much data to go on, at first.
So I went all the way back to 1912, when the first taxi service in Japan started, and researched every last detail since then.
I've already analyzed your car, of course. I have full details on every part, as well as your driving habits, right here in my head.
That's dedication right there. So what are my chances?
Based on today's weather, and the state of the road, I came up with a number.
Unfortunately, you only have about one in a hundred chance of beating me.
One in a hundred... That's nothing.
Do you still wish to take me on, taxi driver?
Suzuki-san! Let's quit while we're ahead! One in a hundred is terrible odds. You know you can't win!
The odds may be against me, but I still have a chance, right?
Where I grew up, you don't just run away when things look hopeless.
You step up to the challenge like a man, and carve out your own destiny.
Damn... That hit me real heavy just now...
Heheh. What a character you are. I love it!
Now I'm truly looking forward to seeing you hang your head in defeat.
Let's see if you can put up a fight!
Hahaha! See? I went and crushed your little hopes there, didn't I?
Call it crass, but to me, nothing feels better than unraveling someone's false perspective. I can't get enough of it!
Oh, but you're welcome to try and play the hero anytime! It's quite entertaining!
Wow. A hundred-to-one shot, and you pulled it off with style.
This is unreal... All the data showed I'd win without a hitch. What went wrong!?
Battles aren't won by data and statistics. The numbers must've clouded your mind.
Ridiculous...
Sorry, Suzuki-san... I never should've doubted you.
Do you see now? Your fate isn't written in stone. You can change it if you try hard enough.
I think it's time you changed yours now.
Okay. I'll do that!
I'm back. And look who I brought with me.
Hey there⑬ Oh, Kiyokawa-kun!
Guys! Is the offer to help me study still on the table?
Where's this coming from all of a sudden?
Yeah, I thought you said it was hopeless.
What are you talking about!? If you give up when things look grim, you'll never get anywhere in life! Now let's start with some flashcards!
...I don't know what you did, Suzuki-san, but it worked.
Oh, I didn't do anything.
All right, all right. I'll help you. But aren't you forgetting something first?
I should probably be apologizing for my behavior from before, huh?
Aha, you got it.
He's finally acting his age.
Let's hope so.
Remember to be sincere about it.
Of course. I'd like to start and end by saying...
Sorry for rufflin' your feathers!
Huh? What the hell kind of apology is that?
My bad! Sorry for rubbin' you the wrong way!
Uh... sorry for wreckin' your expectations?
Sorry for rustlin' your jimmies?
Okay, you can stop now!
It's that highway rest area client again. They asked if you wanted to taste the wine of defeat once more... which I find to be very odd.
(Must be Gentle Nakamura, one of the Devil Killers' Four Kings.)
You know, you should never drink on the job, even if a client suggests it.
Yes, I'm aware. I'll be heading out now.
Hey Suzuki-san! Can I tag along?
(This guy gets everything he wants, doesn't he...)
It's that client from the highway rest area.
(So the Devil Killers are back for more, huh?)
Then I'm on my way.
Mind if I tag along? That way you can teach me how to deal with more clients!
(He obviously knows where I'm going.)
What happened to studying for your Class 2?
Well, both Wada-san and Muramatsu-san seem pretty sure that I can pass now! They gave me their okay!
Did they really?
Yeah, I even aced a practice test! I've been studying my butt off!
Help me out, Hirakawa-san!
Hmm... I'd say you've been making an admirable effort.
Why not take him with you, Suzuki-san? He does need more time in the field.
I'm not sure he'd benefit from this kind of request...
Aww, don't say that! Even if it doesn't seem relevant, I still wanna know how it's done.
You're certainly enthusiastic. Now if that's not dedication, I don't know what is. Wouldn't you say so?
...I guess.
Cool! I'm gonna take that as a yes, then! Now let's jam!
Ready for another day of staring at my brake lights in the distance?
I think you mean the other way around.
You seem pretty confident, Mr. Suzuki! How wonderful! Then let's get this party started!
There are only two out of four Kings left to go. You can do this!
(At least he's not trying to dissuade me like before.)
You beat Crash Kajiwara first, then Cool Yoshimi. I guess that means today you'll be facing...
Which one of you big boys is Mr. Suzuki from Nagasu Taxi?
Ooh, there he is! The second-in-command of the Four Kings... Gentle Nakamura!
What's so gentle about him?
Beats me. But he's a true veteran⑬oldest one on the team. He's the last original Devil Killer, too. Been with 'em from the start.
And don't let his age fool you⑬he's fast as lightning and then some! Not to mention he's racked up tons of wisdom and experience behind the wheel.
You're pretty clued up for a youngster. Not bad, Mr. Suzuki.
Actually, "Mr. Suzuki" is this guy right here!
Ah, so you're the man... You sure you're in the right place? Truth be told, I thought you'd be a little less on in years.
That makes two of us.
Hoho. Don't mistake me for one of those doddering old seniors you see puttering around.
When it comes to driving, experience trumps all else. I've refined my skills over decades, maturing them like a fine wine.
Now I hear you've already bested two of the Four Kings. Is that correct?
That is.
Well, from where I'm standing, those guys might as well be fresh out of driving school.
Just because you know how to hold the wheel and step on the gas doesn't mean you know how to race.
Watch and learn, Mr. Suzuki! Because today's lesson is... how to lose sight of a veteran!
So tell me. How do you find the bitter wine of defeat? A bit too strong for the palate?
Well, I'll pour you as many glasses as you want. Defeat won't get any sweeter, though.
You see, here at Gentle Nakamura's vineyard, we age our sour grapes in tear-soaked barrels, then pour the contents liberally down your throat until you're choking on despair!
Perhaps I took the imagery a bit too far. Now if you'll excuse me...
You did it, Suzuki-san! That's nearly all four Kings!
There's only one left⑬their leader!
How could this be...? I've been racing for decades, doggone it!
...Though, I suppose this turn of events isn't entirely uncalled for. I must say, Nakajima found himself a diamond in the rough.
...Did you just say Nakajima? How do you know our boss?
How? Why, he's the original Devil Killer. The man started this whole gang over twenty years ago.
Wait, you're telling me <Italic>the chief</Italic> started the Devil Killers!? You gotta be joking! He's just an old geezer! ...No offense.
We were all a lot younger twenty years ago. Your boss was a real speed demon back then⑬the fastest in Fukuoka, and maybe even all of Kyushu.
That's just... Nah, my brain can't handle this.
Then... Then tell me why a legendary god of street racing would quit just to start driving taxis around!
Your guess is as good as mine, young man.
Weren't you an original member of his team? Surely you must know something.
Ah, back then I was just a slowpoke. I never really got to talk to the man.
Though, I'm glad I stuck with it. I made it to the Four Kings, after all... Took me long enough.
And now I go losing to a taxi driver. Perhaps my age has finally caught up with me. Some racer I am, eh?
Hey there. I hear you were out showin' Kiyokawa-kun the ropes today, huh?
No, today I was up against the Devil Killers.
Oh? That thing you were doing for the local police? Don't get into any accidents, y'hear?
...Chief, I need to ask you something.
Hmm? And what's that?
Is it true you were the one who founded the Devil Killers?
...Where'd ya hear that?
From Gentle Nakamura, the guy I just raced.
...Looks like the cat's out of the bag. I was thinkin' to have a sit-down with ya one of these days... might as well be now.
When yer young, ya have time to do whatever your heart desires. For me, that was cars. I loved 'em more than anything... well, just about.
Before I knew it, there were a whole bunch of us, motorheads to the core. So I decided to form the Devil Killers.
